newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr bounces, but rate test just delayed.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr bounces, but rate test just delayed.

text.p: The Australian dollar was a 1/3 cent firmer at the midsession although off its highs after its early short covering rally stalled at US$0.7420 resistance.
The currency took off after the Reserve Bank stayed silent at its morning money market operation, confounding intense speculation it would ease policy today.

Traders said those betting on a move had to reverse a few positions, but the overall market remained very short in the confident expectation the bank would ease after its board meeting on August 5. Thus while they saw room for some gains near term, they doubted it could clear the US$0.7375 barrier.

By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the dollar was hovering at US$0.7393/98 having climbed as high as US$0.7423 shortly after the RBA policy window came and went, but was still up on its early US$0.7361/66 and US$0.7348/53 late here Thursday.

Traders said support under US$0.7330 had impressed so far and would probably hold while the market waited for the RBA to make up its mind, but if it were broken a test of the 1996 trough of US$0.7305 would not be far behind.
The currency was broadly firmer on the crosses thanks largely to fund flows out of the mark and Swiss franc and into the dollar bloc in general.
